title: What's the most expensive toilet in the world?
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant discuss the most expensive toilet in the world: a solid gold toilet displayed at Hang Fung Jewelers in Hong Kong, part of a solid gold laboratory display. In early 2008 Hang Fung began melting down parts of the display as gold prices rose, drawing public anger, though the hosts say the solid gold toilet itself was to remain. They then discuss the trend of luxury bathroom upgrades and their home resale value, couples hosting parties in bathrooms, high-end fixtures such as the Neorest toilet (heated seat, lid that opens on approach, cleaning water jet and air dryer) and the UV-tanning Idle Lux shower, and a brief history of toilets from cesspits to trenches to outhouses to modern toilets.

segments.title: Opening and ad read
segments.summary: Opening with an ad read for a camera, then Josh introduces the topic and guest-style banter with Candice Gibson about the most expensive toilet.

segments.title: Solid gold toilet at Hang Fung in Hong Kong
segments.summary: The solid gold toilet is part of a solid gold laboratory display at Hang Fung Jewelers in Hong Kong, the store's biggest attraction. In early 2008 Hang Fung began melting parts of the display because gold prices had risen sharply amid the subprime mortgage crisis, angering the public, but the solid gold toilet was to remain.

segments.title: Luxury bathroom trend and home value
segments.summary: The hosts discuss bathrooms becoming spa-like retreats with marble counters, sunken tubs and chandeliers, and a study saying luxury bath upgrades return a large share of their cost. They note that bathrooms are replacing kitchens as party gathering places, citing a Wall Street Journal article about an engagement party held in a bathroom.

segments.title: High-end toilets and showers
segments.summary: Chuck praises the Neorest toilet, which opens its lid on approach, warms the seat, and cleans and dries the user. They also mention the Idle Lux shower, a stand-up shower with UV lights that tan the user.

segments.title: History of toilets
segments.summary: The hosts joke about the evolution of toilets, from cesspits where people urinated and defecated in open areas, to trenches, to outhouses, to modern high-end toilets like the Neorest.

segments.title: Sign-off and website pointer
segments.summary: Josh points listeners to the HowStuffWorks article on the most expensive toilet and invites feedback at the podcast email address, followed by an ad read.
